steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Lightly grease an 8-inch square baking pan.
Whisk flour, cornmeal, sugar, baking soda, and salt together in a large bowl. Stir in yogurt and eggs until just combined; do not overmix. Pour batter into the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until the center springs back when lightly pressed, 20 to 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Excellent and Healthy Cornbread
raw_recipe.description: This healthy cornbread recipe is made with nonfat yogurt in place of oil. It mixes up in minutes and is ready to enjoy after just 20 minutes in the oven.
raw_recipe.name: Excellent and Healthy Cornbread

review.reviewBody:
This is a simple recipe with delicious results.
I added 1/2 cup liquid honey, next time I'll add just 1/4 cup as it was a little too sweet. It held well together and was great with baked beans.
This is a keeper!

I used greek yogart and had to add probably 1/2 cup of skim milk. Without the milk it was a dry dough than a batter. Even after the milk I still had to spread it into the pan with a spatula. I also used a preheated cast iron skillet with olive oil in the bottom. This gave it a nice crispy bottom crust. Cooking took closer to 15 minutes than 20 minutes. It turned out really well and has a very pleasant texture. It's not crumbly at all and holds together really well.

I substituted 1/2 cup whole wheat flour for half of the white, used unsweetened almond milk instead of yogurt, replaced the sugar with Splenda and poured it into a hot, oiled cast iron skillet to give it a nice chewy, crispie crust. Baked it only 18 minutes and it was great. My husband never asks me for anything because he doesn't want me in the kitchen late into the evening. But this is one recipe that he will ask for. So I will continue to used this recipe. NOTE: For the hot skillet trick, I put a tablespoon or so of olive oil in my cast iron skillet and slide it into the oven while it's preheating and I'm mixing the batter together. When my batter is ready, I pour it directly into the hot skillet. It should sizzle when you do this! Makes for a great texture.

Since other reviewers found this recipe dry and overly dense, I added 1/2 tsp of baking powder to add some lift, substituted 1/4c of honey for the sugar (and might try a bit more next time), and baked at 375 for 15 minutes in 12 muffin tins. This made really decent muffins, but I will try adding more honey next time and I might experiment with some corn kernels. I also used coarse ground corn meal, which likely makes a difference, but the recipe doesn’t specify which kind to use.

It was quick to assemble and came out great. The batter was too thick (maybe since I used Greek yogurt instead of regular?). I used 1/8 c of sugar and 1/8 c of a 1:1 sugar substitute. I added a splash of almond milk and also added garlic & two jalapeños. Baked it for 20 minutes and it came out PERFECT. Served with butter drizzled over. Will keep this recipe.

This cornbread definitely tasted healthy. I have been making Golden Sweet Cornbread, on the site, for years. So, I had a comparison. I read the reviews and saw that some people subbed white whole wheat for all-purpose flour, so I did that. A lot of people mentioned it being dense, so I did 1/2 baking soda and 1/2 baking powder for the baking soda amount. I wanted it more sweet than savory, so I reduced the salt to 1/2 tsp. I made 10 muffins instead of a square. I reduced the temp to 375 and baked them for 18 minutes. I measured out 1 tablespoon of honey and brushed the tops of the warm muffins. The slightly crunchy honey coated top was my favorite part. Although, it was not part of the recipe. Despite doing part baking powder, they were still just a little too dense for my taste.

substituted 1/2 cup whole wheat flour for the white; Added a Tbsp. flaxseed meal....used some of the sugar, but also subbed in about a Tbsp. honey and a teaspoon of vanilla. Also added a half Tbsp. canola oil. All of these made the recipe moist and hopefully a little healthy with the WW flour and flaxseed meal. Baked them as muffins, so lowered the heat to 375 and baked for 17 minutes. They're just right for a dinner muffin with pulled pork or a breakfast muffin...not too sweet, but sweet enough; nice tender crumb and moist!

I love this recipe. Since I am diabetic, I must watch sugar intake. I make another recipe from a diabetic cookbook, but so many steps. Recipe got my eye, because it was made with yogurt (which I make my own to control sugars and preservatives). I took suggestions from other reviewers and added couple items as well: 2 tablespoons honey and applesauce; as well as, 1/2 teaspoon baking powder. Next time I might add 1 teaspoon vanilla. Also not sure if other reviewers meant white whole wheat or whole wheat so I made it with 1/2 cup white whole wheat and 1/2 cup white flour. Cornbread was not dry at all. Also I baked at 400 and crust was too brown, and not quite done inside. It could be my countertop oven, but next time will turn down to 350 and bake longer -- possibly 25 -30 mins, or until done. 

But I will make it again -- very, very tasty and so easy to make. Great with chili, or just as desert after dinner with homemade fruit spread.

This is the only cornbread recipe I'll use from now on. Note that the cooking time was 15 minutes in a well-preheated oven. This is delicious and moist, not greasy like some recipes. I used stevia in place of sugar and the corn completely masked the odd flavor of the stevia. This cornbread is more flavorful than "sweet" so don't let the 1/4 cup of sugar put you off if you like a non-sweet version.
I used White Mountain Bulgarian Yogurt. It is a very tart and almost runny yogurt. My cornbread was very moist and had a great flavor.

I was pleasantly surprised at how good this was - moist, with great texture. I added a slug of honey and a drizzle of vegetable oil to the yogurt before mixing it in to the dry ingredients. I replaced the sugar with granulated Swerve. 

I don't know if it had any impact on the outcome, but I made the batter a few hours before baking, and put it in the fridge until a half-hour before it went in the oven.

Interesting texture, more open structure and moister than most cornbread I've made. Feels somewhat more coarse, but excessively so. Not crumbly at all. Not as sweet as a Northern style, but somewhat sweeter than most Southern style cornbreads. Went together quickly and easily. I'll likely make it again.
I followed it exactly as it is with the exception of the sugar which I didn't have and replaced it with honey. It came out great. I really like it and will make it again. Thank you!

Read the reviews before trying, so I added 1/4 cup of honey, and I substituted unsweetened applesauce for the yogurt. I was very careful to just fold in the batter enough to wet it. So moist and great flavour and sweetness but not too sweet either. We really enjoyed and will make again!

I cooked it for 23 minutes at 400 degrees F and it came out really puffy and a little bit more then golden-brown on top so I probably overcooked it a little bit. Does anyone have any tips for me? -MSZO

This is not as sweet as most cornbread, but I didn't find it dry like others did. I noticed the directions called for beating the eggs (which I did) so I wonder if that made a texture difference. I cooked it for 20 minutes and it bounced back as described. Had a nice crispness to the top. I served it with honey and butter and my guests loved it with the soup we were having.

I made this following the recipe exactly and it was very dry. It needs something and most likely needs milk or butter. I probably should have read the reviews and realized that many have modified the recipe, however, I don't think I want to try it again.
This recipe is lacking something. Up the sugar and/or fat. I had to add butter, a little oil and honey just to get this tolerable. Isn’t the driest I’ve tried but super lacks flavor.
